# Employee Handbook

## 1. Welcome

This handbook sets out the day-to-day policies that apply to every employee.
It is reviewed each January; the version on the intranet is always the
authoritative copy. Nothing in it forms part of your contract of employment
unless your contract says so explicitly.

## 2. Working hours

Core hours are 10:00 to 16:00, Monday to Friday. Outside core hours you may
arrange your remaining time flexibly with your line manager, provided your
contracted weekly hours are met. Time recording is via the HR portal and must
be completed by the last working day of each month.

## 3. Remote work

Up to three days per week may be worked remotely by default. A fully remote
arrangement needs a written agreement with your line manager and a review
every six months. Remote days are not carried over between weeks.

## 4. Annual leave

The leave year runs from 1 April to 31 March. Full-time employees receive 25
days of annual leave plus public holidays. A maximum of 5 unused days may be
carried into the next leave year and must be used by 30 June. Leave requests
go through the HR portal and need your line manager's approval before travel
is booked.

## 5. Sickness absence

Notify your line manager before 09:30 on the first day of absence. A
self-certification form covers the first 7 calendar days; a fit note from a
doctor is required from the 8th day onwards. Occupational sick pay starts
after the probation period and is set out in your contract schedule.

## 6. Travel

Business travel must be booked through the approved travel portal. Standard
class applies to journeys under 3 hours; longer journeys may be booked in the
next class up. Taxis are only reimbursed where public transport is
impractical or for journeys after 22:00.

## 7. Expenses

Submit claims through the finance portal within 30 days of the spend, with a
photographed receipt for every line. Card statements are not accepted as
receipts. Any single expense claim above £250 requires written approval from
a director before it is submitted, and reimbursement is paid with the next
payroll run. Alcohol is never reimbursable.

## 8. Equipment

Standard issue is a laptop, monitor, keyboard and headset. Replacement
hardware is on a 4-year cycle. Faults are reported through the IT service
desk; do not attempt repairs yourself. Personal devices must not hold
customer data under any circumstances.

## 9. Learning and development

Each employee has an annual professional development budget of £1,200, which
may be spent on courses, conferences or certifications agreed with your line
manager. Unused budget does not roll over. Study leave of up to 3 days per
year is available for accredited examinations.

## 10. Leaving the company

Notice periods are set out in your contract. On your last day return all
equipment and passes to the IT service desk. Accrued but untaken leave is
paid in your final payroll; any negative leave balance is deducted the same
way.
